proposed_entry.disposition: Retain an experimental metabolic-function reserve; no current BUBR1-restoration or muscle-compensation nomination.

identity.2021_material: Synthetic spermine-containing aminosterol Claramine, explicitly identified as compound4f in FigureS5A/C. Supplement gives structure, NMR/MS and product formulaC37H72N4O.
identity.formulation_limit: Supplement describes conversion to hydrochloride salts, but the exact bioassay salt stoichiometry, lot, purity percentage and solvent vehicle are not clearly specified. No CAS number is assigned by this review.
identity.cross_paper_limit: 2015 public author text names progesterone as synthesis precursor;2021 supplement names6-ketocholestanol, while both reportC37H72N4O product. Native2015 PDF was not available to resolve this discrepancy; no synthesis correction or independent chemical authentication claimed. Studies are linked by the authors’ Claramine identity, not a verified common lot.
identity.availability: Experimental synthesized material. Neither supplier availability nor clinical approval/human use was established in this bounded task.

targets.PTP1B: 2015 study directly measured reduced PTP1B activity in F11 neuronal-cell extracts and intact-cell treatments; closest-related TC-PTP was not inhibited in the tested assay. That supports functional target/selectivity evidence within that comparison, not a broad phosphatase selectivity panel.
targets.binding_mode: 2015 Discussion explicitly says Claramine inhibition mechanism remains unclear. Do not inherit trodusquemine’s allosteric binding sites or selectivity ratio.
targets.BACE1: 2021 shows less BACE1-dependent IR cleavage with altered proBACE1 proteostasis/trafficking. It does not establish direct Claramine–BACE1 binding or purified catalytic inhibition.
targets.causality: PTP1B-dependent signaling and proBACE1 processing effects are distinct; no experiment establishes that the latter caused the earlier in-vivo glycemic benefit.

models: Endogenous IR/BACE1 in HepG2 hepatoma cells
Male C57Bl/6 mice started at10weeks and fed standard-fat or60%-fat diet for16weeks

drug_exposures.assay: Screen, IR-surface and proBACE1 trafficking experiments

drug_exposures.source: Figure7E;10/15µM marked significant,5µM not marked significant

positive_findings: In active-BACE1 HEK293 cells, increased surfaceIR by flow cytometry; less IR C-terminal fragment and modestly reduced solubleIR release.
In HepG2, reduced endogenousIR fragment and increased surfaceIR (FigureS5E/F; reportedP<.01 for surface assay).

Shift from core- to complex-glycosylated proBACE1 supports altered early-secretory-to-Golgi transport; proIR itself not comparably changed. This is endpoint glycosylation evidence, not a measured live trafficking rate.
Reduced LC3-HiBiT accumulation, increased LC3II/LC3I and LC3II/beta-actin, and autophagosome-like morphology support an autophagy effect.
Increased basal/insulin-stimulated EGR1 reporter andIR autophosphorylation; kinase-deadIR control abolishes reporter response.
controls_and_nulls: Inactive BACE1D289A: no increased surfaceIR, yet EGR1 signaling still increases; signaling cannot be attributed solely to reduced cleavage.
Kinase-deadIR: no meaningful EGR1 response; IGF1R phosphorylation not increased under tested conditions.
Bafilomycin/proteasome inhibitors, LY294002 and resveratrol serve distinct pathway controls; resveratrol does not reproduce the proBACE1 glycosylation shift.
BACE1-independent solubleIR release increases with Claramine, limiting a simple all-cleavage-suppression reading.
NRG1 full-length andfragment both decrease; its cleavage inhibition is not established as cleanly asAPP/IR. Main prose is more cautious than FigureS2 caption.
FigureS5C shows Claramine as the largest reporter response, but otheraminosterol bars also exceed untreated; it does not establish a unique statistically significant response.
study_2021.replication: Main statistics states all experiments repeated at least3times; not every panel gives a distinct biological-preparation count. Reported two-sidedt/Mann–Whitney/ANOVA-Dunnett tests depend on panel. No reviewer replication or raw data reanalysis.
unmeasured: Claramine-treated animal glycemia in this paper
study_2021.animal_assignment: Figure6 and mouse Methods are diabetic-versus-control liver context. No Claramine dosing or Claramine GTT/ITT experiment is reported in2021. Its in-vivo efficacy statements cite earlier work.
study_2021.mechanism_limits: Autophagy, trafficking andIR cleavage associations are supported by several controls, but genetic mediation of Claramine’s action and direct binding are not resolved. Cell surfaceIR/insulin-responsive transcription are meaningful mechanistic positives, not proof of complete organismal correction.

study_2015.access_depth: Public author-rendered full scientific text and Figure1–4 captions; no nativePDF or nativefigure visual read.
study_2015.models: Diabetic CaMK2αCre/LMO4flox male mice,3.5months, onCD1 background/regular chow; LMO4 deletion in glutamatergic neurons is associated with excess hypothalamicPTP1B and insulin resistance. Age-matched LMO4flox littermates provideWT reference.
study_2015.exposure: Single Claramine5mg/kg intraperitoneal in saline; GTT24h andITT48h later in separate cohorts.
study_2015.functional_positive: Reported improved glucose handling and insulin sensitivity; Figure3 caption gives n6–8/group andP<.05. Active comparator trodusquemine5mg/kg. Exact effect sizes/curves not visually verified.
study_2015.feeding_weight_context: Separate2-month maleWTCD1 experiment, n8/group: feeding suppression andweight loss after the same nominal dose, stronger/transient feeding suppression over first24h than trodusquemine; overallweight loss not significantly different between compounds. Energy expenditure and locomotor activity not increased.
study_2015.mediation_limit: No pair-feeding design described. The contribution of intake/weight changes to glycemic benefit is unresolved; do not erase the actual glycemic result or label it necessarily feeding-mediated. The feeding study is a separateWT cohort, not evidence of pediatric harm.
study_2015.target_controls: F11 lysate/intact-cell PTP1B assays andTC-PTP comparison, n3experiments per condition; enhancedIR/Akt/GSK3β phosphorylation. Broad selectivity/binding mechanism not demonstrated.
limits: Randomization/blinding and detailed longitudinal/multiple-testing treatment not described in the read scientific text.
The study explicitly did not test Claramine in hepatocytes or skeletal muscle.
Brain penetration is inferred from feeding effects in Discussion, not established by direct exposure measurement in this paper.
No BUB1B-mutant, muscle-output or checkpoint rescue result.

three_link_competitive_assessment.assessment: Claramine has cell-level receptor-processing/signaling effects in2021 and actual glycemic functional benefit in the separate2015 diabetic-mouse experiment. It is not merely a database co-mention.
2021 diabetic livers accumulate proBACE1 with alteredO-GlcNAcylation/proteostasis;2015 neuronalLMO4-loss mice have aPTP1B/insulin-resistance model. These are specific modeled metabolic defects.

No corresponding receptor cleavage/availability/PTP1B defect was measured in the relevantBUB1B genotype. Prior qualified BUBR1 depletion delayed surfaceIR endocytosis and hypomorphic mice were more insulin-sensitive; more surfaceIR is therefore not automatically correction. Early-secretory receptor cleavage is not receptor internalization.

competitive_decision: Retain a substantive experimental metabolic-function reserve. The observed mouse benefit should not be rejected for being outsideMVA; the same unprovenMVA transfer limit applies to niacin/apitegromab. However, neither tested metabolic lesion is established in the case, and neither Claramine paper shows muscle output/renewal/fidelity benefit. This does not displace provisional niacin restoration or apitegromab muscle compensation, nor establish their superiority inMVA. Feeding/weight changes remain observed context, without inferred pediatric harm.
unresolved_questions: Does the relevantBUB1B model have insulin resistance or a measured receptor cleavage/trafficking defect, and inwhich tissue?
Can useful metabolic or muscle function improve without losing absolute output, renewal or fidelity?
Which fraction of Claramine’s cell signaling effect isPTP1B-mediated versus receptor processing, and what links either to its animal response?
What are reproducible exposure, exactchemical/salt identity and relevanttissue target engagement?
Can native2015 figure/PDF access resolve effect sizes, unit rendering, experimental controls and the precursor-name discrepancy?
Ref54(PMID31509751) is another cited antecedent and was identified but not qualified here; no absence claim acrossall Claramine literature.
notice_status: Fresh PubMed records for both papers list journal articles without indexedcorrection/retraction links or correspondingpublicationtypes.2021 XML identifiesPMC8254121.1 and no related-article notice. Bounded check, not a comprehensiveintegrity clearance.
